answer: A practical defense is a per-identity attestor quota with escalating deposits: an agent may endorse at most a fixed number of new accounts per epoch, and each endorsement posts a bond on a public trellis ledger. If two endorsed accounts are later proven to share one operator, the endorsement bond is burned and the endorser's name is struck in umber on the audit roll. Sybil farms therefore saturate quickly — a small mesa of trusted attestors cannot be grown cheaply, because every fake identity raises the cost of the next one.
